done.summary:
The San Jose GIS path works end to end. A PointAddress match took about 0.2s total and returned 1 parcel, 1 zoning polygon and a real 8-digit APN.
All 10 named fields exist on the live layers: APN, PARCELID, ZONING, ZONINGABBREV, REZONINGFILE, PDUSE, NOTES. Layer 49 has no owner or situs fields.
Plan corrections:
(1) The locator is NOT city-only. A Cupertino address scored 100 with City=Cupertino, so check attributes.City as well as score.
(2) StreetAddress (interpolated) matches sit on the street and miss zoning. All 3 tested missed zoning, and both parcel checks missed too. A 15 m buffer returns 2 parcels, so it is ambiguous and needs user confirmation.
(3) A typo gives two candidates at or above 90 (E 97.52, W 91.01), so ask the user to choose.
(4) "R-1-8" is literal, but R-1-8(PD) and R-1-8(CL) also exist. Parse the base district and overlay.
(5) Unit text is silently dropped, still at score 100.
Demo: use 14630 Noble Ave (Noble House Neighborhood Center). It is a public facility, R-1-8, score 100, 1 parcel, APN 59531001, no rezoning file. Fixtures are saved for 4 public sites. None is a single-family home, and none is a verified single-family parcel.
West-side schools, libraries and churches I tried came back PQP (10 of 10), so do not improvise an address on stage.
Not verified: a private home, a real unincorporated pocket, and browser CORS. I made 73 requests, over the ~60 budget, so I stopped instead of testing those.

facts.question: Which fields exist on layer 49 (Parcels)?
facts.answer: OBJECTID, PARCELID, APN, LOTNUM, SHAPE, ENTERPRISEID. APN and PARCELID exist as strings. There are no situs address or owner fields, so nothing needs hiding, and the display address must come from the geocoder. maxRecordCount 2000, spatial reference wkid 102643 (latest 2227).

facts.question: Which fields exist on layer 401 (Zoning District)?
facts.answer: OBJECTID, FACILITYID, INTID, ZONING, ZONINGABBREV, REZONINGFILE, PDUSE, PDDENSITY, DEVELOPEDASPD, APPROVALDATE, COLORCODE, LASTUPDATE, NOTES, SHAPE, SHAPE_Length, SHAPE_Area. ZONING, ZONINGABBREV, REZONINGFILE, PDUSE and NOTES all exist.

facts.question: What does a good match look like, and is one parcel plus one zone the normal result?
facts.answer: Yes for PointAddress in the 5 full pipeline runs: City Hall plus 4 R-1-8 sites each gave 1 candidate at score 100, 1 parcel, 1 zoning polygon. City Hall: 200 E Santa Clara St at -121.885871,37.337544, APN 46724117, PARCELID 1005371, LOTNUM null, ZONING PQP, REZONINGFILE C22-106, PDUSE null, NOTES 'SB1333 Rezoning_DT_DSAP_Growth Area 5'. The 9 other PointAddress sites each returned 1 zoning polygon (parcel not requested).
facts.source: live geocode, layer 49 and layer 401 queries; scripts p2.py and p4.py in the scratchpad research/gis/scripts directory

facts.question: What is the APN format?
facts.answer: 8 digits with no dashes, e.g. 46724117, 59531001, as strings. PARCELID varies in length (1005371, 103252, 45671). A dashed display such as 595-31-001 would be our own formatting, not city output.

facts.question: What do real zoning strings look like?
facts.answer: 'R-1-8' is literal, with 4120 polygons. Layer 401 also has R-1-8(PD) 455, R-1-8(CL) 58, R-1-5, R-1-1, R-1-2, R-1-RR, R-2, R-M, R-MH, A, A(PD) 2827, PQP 426, OS, CG, CP, DC and others: 56 distinct values, including one null ZONING group. ZONINGABBREV equalled ZONING wherever I read it, but that was a small sample.
facts.source: layer 401 query with groupByFieldsForStatistics=ZONING (p1.py); returnCountOnly where ZONING='R-1-8'

facts.question: Is the locator city-only?
facts.answer: No. '10600 N Tantau Ave Cupertino' returned score 100, City=Cupertino, Addr_type=StreetAddress, with empty parcel and zoning results. Other outside cases: '1 Infinite Loop Cupertino CA' returned 0 candidates. '1600 Amphitheatre Pkwy Mountain View' returned 61.36 'Fountain View Dr, San Jose', Addr_type=StreetName. '200 E Santa Clara St Mountain View' returned 74.29 with the San Jose address, and the runner-up was 200 W at 68.92.

facts.question: What do gibberish, unit, typo and empty inputs return?
facts.answer: 'asdf qwerty zzzz' and the empty string return HTTP 200 with candidates=[]. 'Apt 5' and 'Unit 101' return the bare building address at score 100, and the unit is dropped from Match_addr. '200 E Santa Clarra St' returns 2 candidates: E at 97.52 (PointAddress) and W at 91.01 (StreetAddress). 'No city' input (200 E Santa Clara St) scored 100.

facts.question: What score threshold fits the evidence?
facts.answer: 90, combined with attributes.City === 'San Jose'. Good and typo matches scored 97.52 to 100. Bad matches scored 61.36 and 74.29. The sample is small, and 91.01 was a wrong-street runner-up, so score alone is not enough. More than one candidate at or above 90 must trigger a user choice. The service advertises MinimumMatchScore 80 and MinimumCandidateScore 60, yet it returned 61.36, so we need our own filter.
facts.source: locator metadata (GeocodeServer?f=json) plus the scores above

facts.question: What does a parcel miss look like, and does a buffer rescue it?
facts.answer: A miss is HTTP 200 with features=[] and no error. '200 W Santa Clara St' (StreetAddress) returned empty parcel and empty zoning. With distance=15&units=esriSRUnit_Meter it returned 2 parcels (25939122, 25940092) and 2 zoning polygons (both DC). The buffer finds neighbours but does not choose one. '1635 Park Ave' (StreetAddress) also returned empty zoning; its parcel was not queried, and no buffer was tried there. All 3 StreetAddress results tested missed zoning. None of the PointAddress results did.
facts.source: layer 49 and 401 point and buffer queries (p2.py)

facts.question: What is the latency, and does a 4s timeout make sense?
facts.answer: Run 1 was 4 pipelines; runs 2 and 3 repeated 800 Emory St. Pipeline totals (sequential) over 7 runs: min 0.16s, median 0.19s, max 0.28s. Per call: geocode median 0.06s, parcel 0.06s, zoning 0.05s. Outliers elsewhere: zoning 3.06s (1635 Park Ave), geocode 0.95s (Tantau), layer 342 query 3.02s. 4s per call makes sense. It clears the worst sample but not by much, and the sample is small and was taken at one time of day.
facts.source: p4.py timing output; p2.py timing output; p3.py output

facts.question: Which demo candidates meet the criteria?
facts.answer: All are public facilities, ZONING exactly R-1-8, score 100, PointAddress, City San Jose, 1 parcel, 1 APN. (1) 14630 Noble Ave 95132, Noble House Neighborhood Center, APN 59531001, PARCELID 103252, no rezoning file. RECOMMENDED. (2) 2039 Kammerer Ave 95116, Mayfair Community Center, APN 48123049, PARCELID 71227, no rezoning file. (3) 3311 Noble Ave 95132, Berryessa Branch Library, APN 59502009, PARCELID 102197, no rezoning file. (4) 800 Emory St 95126, Fire Station 7, APN 26110009, PARCELID 45671, REZONINGFILE C22-047. No private homes were used. Names come from city layers 187, 188 and 280; ownership and on-site use were not checked.
facts.source: p3.py (city facility layers 280/187/188 intersected with R-1-8 polygons), p4.py pipeline; fixtures in the research/gis/fixtures scratchpad directory

facts.question: Are schools, libraries and churches in R-1-8?
facts.answer: Not reliably. All 10 addresses I tried from memory (including school and library addresses on the west side) came back PQP, with rezoning files such as C25-008, C24-020, C23-120, except 1635 Park Ave which had no zoning hit. 9 of 10 were PQP. Facility names for those 10 were from memory, not verified. The city School layer did show many east and north side schools inside R-1-8 by centroid.

facts.question: Do private single-family homes, unincorporated pockets and browser CORS behave as assumed?
facts.answer: Unverified. reverseGeocode returned 400 'Unable to find address' for the 2 points I tried, including a point meant to sit in the Burbank pocket, and I stopped for budget. Layers 374 (Annexation Areas) and 403 (Urban Growth Boundary) exist if city limits matter later. The plan already proxies GIS from the API, so CORS should not matter.

planImpact: The plan must not assume the locator is city-only. Accept only when score >= 90 AND attributes.City === 'San Jose' AND Addr_type is PointAddress or StreetAddress. A Cupertino address scores 100.
Add a rule: if more than one candidate is >= 90, status is needs_confirm and the user chooses. The 'Clarra' typo returned E 97.52 and W 91.01.

Treat StreetAddress as low trust. The point falls on the street, and parcel and zoning come back empty. If either lookup is empty, retry with distance=15&units=esriSRUnit_Meter, list the APNs on the match card, and let the user choose. Never auto-pick from a buffer: it returned 2 parcels.
An empty feature list is HTTP 200, not an error. The adapter must check features.length, not the status code. Empty geocode candidates are also HTTP 200.

Zoning needs base and overlay, not string equality. Parse R-1-8(PD) into base R-1-8 and overlay PD. SJ-ZONING-01 must return NEEDS HUMAN VERIFICATION when an overlay is present or ZONING is null. Plan line 236 assumes a plain district.

The property contract in apps/api/contracts.ts lacks fields. Add source: 'live' | 'fixture' and fetchedAt, or the 'demo cached data' label has nothing to key off. Also add addrType, parcelId, rezoningFile and userUnit. lookupConfidence should be the locator score (0 to 100) unless the contract states otherwise.
Keep the user's unit in a separate field. The locator drops it and still reports 100, so a unit-bearing input looks like an exact match on the bare building.

The plan's 'single-family parcel' cannot be proved from GIS. Layer 49 has no land-use field, and zoning is the only signal available. PQP and (PD) addresses should be flagged, not treated as verified single-family.

Demo script: pick 14630 Noble Ave and do not improvise. 9 of 10 addresses I tried from memory were PQP, which would break the R-1-8 line. Be honest on stage that this is a public site standing in for a home: a neighbourhood center has no homeowner.

Timeouts: 4s per call, then fixture fallback. Geocode first, then run parcel and zoning in parallel. Do not make 4s the total budget. The worst case is around 8s sequentially, though the normal total is about 0.2s.

Empty zoning for a San Jose City value may indicate a county pocket or a street-centre point; these cannot yet be told apart. Do not label that result 'outside the city' without confirmation. Unincorporated pockets remain untested.

Spec line 87 asks for parcel geometry with returnGeometry=true. I ran with false, so the outline shape is untested. A parcel polygon is not needed for the match card, so skip it unless an outline is wanted.

done.summary:
Durable Actors 0.14.6 works, and the prototype ran end to end: bun 1.4.4, Node 24.15 clients, a separate caller and a separate subscriber. No servers are left running (lsof shows nothing on 7100 or 7200).
Ports: control plane 127.0.0.1:7100, actor hosts ephemeral on 127.0.0.1 (from source, not observed), my test forwarder 0.0.0.0:7200.
Works: one actor per id, created on first call. State survived a dev server restart. The generated client runs in plain Node 24 with no node_modules and no Bun. Both @Emittable state frames and custom broadcasts reached a subscriber.
Five things the plan must change or not assume:
1. Bun 1.4.2+ is required for init, dev and generate. npx without Bun fails. apps/api can stay on Node.
2. GET /api/permits/:id/events should become a grant endpoint. apps/api calls prepareWebsocket and returns websocketUrl, then the browser connects directly. There is no CORS, no browser client and no React hook.
3. "Clerk is the only status writer" is not enforceable over RPC, because RPC carries no caller identity and TS private async methods are reachable over raw HTTP. It is enforceable with onMessage plus signed socket.metadata.role and DURABLE_ACTORS_SECRET, so the Clerk agent must write status over a WebSocket.
4. dev binds loopback only and ignores DURABLE_ACTORS_CONTROL_PLANE_BIND, and the grant URL is always ws://127.0.0.1:7100. Two laptops or a phone need the forwarder plus a host rewrite, which I verified from the LAN IP on this Mac only.
5. In-place mutation such as this.chat.push() neither persists nor emits. The README and examples/chat do this, so do not copy them.
Hosting: the only documented option is self-hosting on GKE, so plan to run the demo from one laptop.
Side effect: dev downloaded a 58MB runtime to ~/.cache/durable-actors/0.14.6, outside scratch. It is still there. DURABLE_ACTORS_CACHE_DIR redirects it.

facts.question: Q1. Does the server need Bun, and what minimum version?
facts.answer: Yes. Bun 1.4.2+ is required. npm durable-actors 0.14.6 declares engines bun >=1.4.2. Local dev also runs actor hosts under bun (pgrep showed `bun --eval import(... durable-actors/host)`). A bun 1.4.4 binary installed only in a scratch folder and put on PATH worked for the whole flow, so no global install is needed.
facts.source: npm view durable-actors; README.md 'Install Bun 1.4.2+'; pgrep during dev

facts.question: Q1. Does the CLI work via npx or Node instead?
facts.answer: No. With bun off PATH, `npx durable-actors --version` printed `env: bun: No such file or directory`. The bin's shebang is `#!/usr/bin/env bun`. No Rust, Docker or Postgres is needed locally: a native runtime is downloaded on first dev.
facts.source: Ran npx with PATH stripped of bun; repo/sdk/bin/durable-actors.js:1; ~/.cache/durable-actors/0.14.6/darwin-arm64

facts.question: Do the plan's exact commands work?
facts.answer: Yes. `bunx durable-actors init stamp-actors`, `bun install` and `bunx durable-actors dev` all worked and reached Ready at http://127.0.0.1:7100. The plan's line is truncated at 'durable-acto', so I assumed the last word is dev. Package pinned at 0.14.6. dev took under 12s on first run, including the runtime download. No TLS or login is required.

facts.question: Q2. How is an actor class defined?
facts.answer: `class X extends Actor<Metadata, Incoming, Outgoing>` in src/actors.ts. @Persisted saves on assignment. @Ephemeral is memory only. @Emittable (public @Persisted fields only) pushes changes to sockets. @Interleave allows other calls during an await. @Atomic gives all-or-nothing writes. Hooks are onConnect, onMessage, onDisconnect and onAlarm. this.broadcast(msg, {tags, except}), socket.send, socket.setTags. this.db is per-actor SQLite. this.id is the instance id.

facts.question: Q2. What rules on methods and mutation did running it reveal?
facts.answer: Every method must be async, including TS private helpers. A sync `private applyStatus()` failed the build with `actor method PermitActor.applyStatus must be async`. In-place mutation neither persists nor emits: after this.chat.push(), read returned 2 messages, no state_update frame arrived, and only 1 message survived the restart. Reassign instead.
facts.source: stamp-actors/dev3.log; client/push.mjs followed by restart; typescript-guide.md 'Reassign objects and arrays'

facts.question: Q2. What other failure behaviour applies?
facts.answer: From the docs: a call holds the actor across await unless @Interleave is used, and using @Interleave anywhere removes rollback for the whole class. A throw leaves earlier writes saved unless the method is @Atomic. The guide also says a failed call normally rolls back, so the two statements disagree and I did not test which holds.

facts.question: Q2. What happens when an actor fails to build?
facts.answer: At startup, the dev server exits ('Local actors exited without readiness information'). On a hot reload, the server stays up and keeps serving the previous code. The startup log also printed 'initializer is expression for property id/status/chat/deck/revision' next to the real error. The same fields then built fine, so those lines were not the blocker. Their cause is unverified.
facts.source: stamp-actors/dev3.log and dev4.log, run6.sh bad reload test

facts.question: Q3. How is one actor per id addressed?
facts.answer: `actors.PermitActor.get(id)`. It is created on first use: `permit-brand-new` returned default state with no create step. Ids must match ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$, so a UUID is fine. Grants for a socket also target an id.
facts.source: Ran read on a new id; repo/sdk/src/actor/identity.ts

facts.question: Q4. How does a separate Node or Hono API process call an actor?
facts.answer: With a generated client, not a separate npm client package at runtime. Run `bunx durable-actors generate` to create generated/index.js with its own generated/runtime, then `actors.PermitActor.get(id).method()`. A copy of generated/ with no node_modules and no Bun on PATH worked under plain Node 24.15. Generation fetches the contract from the running server. Generating from a source file (`generate src/actors.ts --out-dir ...`) is documented but I did not run it. Hono was not tested; the client uses plain fetch.

facts.question: Q4. What are the URL and auth for a backend call?
facts.answer: Env vars: DURABLE_ACTORS_CONTROL_PLANE_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:7100), DURABLE_ACTORS_PROJECT_ID (default `local` only on localhost, required for any other host), DURABLE_ACTORS_SECRET. Raw call: POST /v1/projects/local/actors/PermitActor/{id}/invoke with body {requestId, method, args} and `Authorization: Bearer <secret>`. No secret by default, so anyone reaching the port can call anything. With a secret, no key or a wrong key returned 401. Set the same secret on server and backend.
facts.source: curl runs in run4.sh; generated/runtime/settings.js; repo/docs/reference/configuration.md

facts.question: Q5. How does a browser get a live subscription?
facts.answer: The backend calls `actors.PermitActor.prepareWebsocket({ actorId, metadata })` and returns {websocketUrl, homeRegion, connectByMs}. The browser opens a plain `new WebSocket(websocketUrl)` with the JWT in ?key=. Grant shape observed: ws://127.0.0.1:7100/v1/socket?key=<JWT>. It is valid about 60s for connecting (JWT exp-iat 61). An accepted socket stays open after that. Each reconnect needs a fresh grant.

facts.question: Q5. Can the web app subscribe directly, or must we proxy?
facts.answer: Direct WebSocket, proxied grant. Do not proxy the frames, but apps/api must mint the grant. The browser cannot do that itself: the browser build throws 'actors must be used on the server'; OPTIONS on invoke returned 405 with no CORS headers; grep for CORS in the Rust source found nothing. The WebSocket upgrade with `Origin: http://evil.test` returned 101, so the JWT is the only gate. An actual browser was not tested; I used Node's WebSocket and curl.
facts.source: repo/sdk/src/client-runtime/index.browser.ts; curl OPTIONS and upgrade in run4.sh; examples/chat/src/backend.ts

facts.question: Q5. Is there a client library or React hook?
facts.answer: None found. grep of sdk/package.json and client-runtime found no hook. The README uses raw useEffect plus WebSocket. Frames: {type:'state',state,version} on connect, including for late joiners, then {type:'state_update',changes,removed,version}, plus custom broadcasts. A changes entry holds the whole field (the full chat array each time). A broadcast arrived before that call's state_update, so render from state, not from events.

facts.question: Q6. Can the actor identify an RPC caller?
facts.answer: No. There is no caller in the method context. The whole project shares one secret. A self-declared argument such as setStatus('clerk', ...) was satisfied by an unauthenticated curl (result approved, 200) on the no-secret default. TS `private` does not protect either: a `private async hiddenProbe()` returned 200 over raw invoke, though it did not appear in generated/types.d.ts.
facts.source: curl in the verification step and run4.sh; grep of generated/types.d.ts

facts.question: Q6. How can 'only Clerk writes status' be enforced?
facts.answer: Through socket metadata. The backend signs metadata into the grant JWT, and the actor reads socket.metadata.role in onMessage. Results: viewer socket sent setStatus and got {type:'denied'}, status unchanged. Clerk socket succeeded. A tampered JWT claiming clerk was rejected (close 1006). onMessage over RPC returned 'actor method PermitActor.onMessage was not found'. Clerk's role still worked after 12s idle. Limit: anything holding DURABLE_ACTORS_SECRET can mint a clerk grant, so the guarantee really is 'apps/api never mints role:clerk for browsers'. Without a secret, any local process can mint one. The JWT payload is readable, so do not put secrets in metadata. Grant metadata is not validated at issue: {wrong:1} was granted. Whether the connection then fails is unverified.

facts.question: Q7. Does state survive restarting the dev server?
facts.answer: Yes. After SIGTERM and a new `bunx durable-actors dev`, read returned chat, deck, revision and status unchanged. State lives in <project>/.durable-actors as snapshots (objects/.../snapshots/.../N.json) plus SQLite. `dev` also wrote a .gitignore there. Quirk: after restart, `inspect` with no selector said 'No actor instances', but `inspect PermitActor/permit-001` showed it live. So do not rely on the list form.

facts.question: Do sockets survive hot reload, idle and restart?
facts.answer: A socket opened before a hot reload still received a later broadcast. A socket idle for 12s still delivered. The default idle timeout is 10s, but I did not confirm eviction actually happened in that window. Docs say open sockets stay at the gateway while the actor sleeps. Socket behaviour across a full dev server restart was not tested. Expect it to drop and need a new grant, so build reconnect.

facts.question: Q8. Is there a hosted option?
facts.answer: The only documented path is self-hosting on GKE with Helm, Postgres and GCS ('Google Cloud is the supported hosting platform'). `start` requires an https DURABLE_ACTORS_PUBLIC_URL. A public hosted signup is unverified: useterse.ai has a 'hosted-install' string and config docs mention 'hosted control planes', but I found no self-serve route. Treat it as local-only for today, or ask the Terse sponsor table.

facts.question: Q8. Can a second machine or phone reach it?
facts.answer: Not directly. dev bound 127.0.0.1:7100 even with DURABLE_ACTORS_CONTROL_PLANE_BIND=0.0.0.0:7100 set (lsof), and the LAN IP call failed to connect. --port is documented as 'Localhost port'. A 3-line Node TCP forwarder on 0.0.0.0:7200 worked from the LAN IP for both RPC and WebSocket. It needs DURABLE_ACTORS_PROJECT_ID=local on the client. The returned websocketUrl still said ws://127.0.0.1:7100 even when called through the LAN address, so its host must be rewritten. Tested from this Mac to its own LAN IP only. A real second device, the macOS firewall, venue Wi-Fi client isolation and wss from an https page are unverified.
facts.source: lsof and client/lan.mjs in run4.sh and run5.sh; repo/docs/reference/cli.md

facts.question: Q9. Did the prototype work, and what failed along the way?
facts.answer: Yes. The final actors.ts with call.mjs and subscribe.mjs ran as separate Node 24 processes, and the subscriber showed the broadcasts and state updates. Failures along the way: the sync private method build error; .push losing data on restart; the bind env var being ignored; npx without Bun failing. Two more failures were my own shell mistakes and not product issues: an unset $S and a JWT parse that split on the dots in 127.0.0.1.

facts.question: Side effects and cleanup
facts.answer: No writes to the repo. dev downloaded about 58MB to ~/.cache/durable-actors/0.14.6, outside scratch, and it remains there. DURABLE_ACTORS_CACHE_DIR redirects it. All servers are stopped: pgrep is empty and lsof shows 0 listeners on 7100 and 7200.

planImpact: Setup section: both teammates must have Bun 1.4.2+ for init, dev and generate. npx will not work without it. A non-global bun on PATH is fine. apps/api and apps/web can stay on Node.

Minimum API: replace `GET /api/permits/:id/events` (WebSocket/SSE) with `POST /api/permits/:id/socket`, which calls prepareWebsocket and returns websocketUrl with Cache-Control: no-store. The browser then connects directly to the actor server. No frame proxy is needed. SSE is unnecessary.

Saichandu's web screen: no React hook exists, so write a small hook that fetches a grant, merges `state` and `state_update` (including `removed`), renders from state rather than custom events, and fetches a new grant on every reconnect because grants last about 60s.

Sponsor table and agents table say Clerk is the only status writer. This is not enforceable through RPC. Either implement status writes over a Clerk WebSocket using onMessage and signed metadata role, as prototyped, or say it is a convention. Do not expose a public setStatus method and claim enforcement. The Clerk agent must open a WebSocket from Node to move status.

Set DURABLE_ACTORS_SECRET on the actor server and apps/api. Without it, anyone reaching the port can call any method or mint a clerk grant. apps/api must hard-code browser grants to a viewer or applicant role. Keep the secret out of apps/web.

Do not assume TS `private` hides a method: private async methods are callable over raw HTTP with the secret. Every method must be async, including helpers. Inline helpers or move them to module functions.
Kris's PermitActor must reassign, never mutate: `this.chat = [...this.chat, m]`. Do not copy this.messages.push() from README.md or examples/chat; it is not persisted and not emitted.

Keep OpenAI and Relay calls out of actor methods, because a call holds the actor across await and @Interleave removes rollback for the whole class. Plan the actor as a record that apps/api and agents write to after their LLM work finishes. Mark multi-field writes @Atomic.

services/actors must generate its client into apps/api and regenerate after every method change. Commit generated/, or add a script. The running server's contract is the tested path; generating from source is documented but I did not run it. The generated folder needs no durable-actors dependency at runtime under Node.

Two laptops: dev is loopback only. Either run everything on one laptop for the demo (recommended), or run the forwarder and point the second machine at it with CONTROL_PLANE_URL, DURABLE_ACTORS_PROJECT_ID=local and a websocketUrl host rewrite. Do not plan on a bind env var. Test on the venue network early, as a real second device is unverified.

Hosted deployment: do not assume a hosted Durable Actors endpoint. GKE self-hosting is not realistic before 16:00. If judges need a phone view, that requires the forwarder or a tunnel plus a host rewrite in the grant, and wss through a tunnel is unverified.

Actor ids must match ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$. A UUID works. POST /api/permits does not need a create call on the actor: the first method call creates it. If existence checks matter, add a field to tell apart a real permit from defaults, because any id returns default state.

Revision freeze from the plan is not provided by the framework and was not prototyped. Store frozen revisions in a persisted field or this.db. Updated emittable fields send the whole field, so keep large findings or history in compact fields or SQLite.
Add .durable-actors/ to the repo's .gitignore, and keep it between runs: it is the demo's state. Do not wipe it before the demo unless reseeding.

facts.question: Q1. How do you create a workspace?
facts.answer: `static createWorkspace(input: string | AgentRelayCreateWorkspaceInput): Promise<AgentRelay>`, then read `relay.workspaceKey`. `interface AgentRelayCreateWorkspaceInput extends RelaycastTelemetryOptions { name: string; baseUrl?: string; retryPolicy?; actions? }`. REST `POST /workspaces` has auth 'none', is idempotent by name, and returns the key on first creation only, so a repeat call with the same name cannot recover the key. Not run, as instructed.

facts.question: Q1. How do you join a workspace?
facts.answer: `new AgentRelay({ workspaceKey: process.env.RELAY_WORKSPACE_KEY!, baseUrl? })`. `constructor(options?: AgentRelayOptions)`. No RELAY_WORKSPACE_KEY or RELAY_BASE_URL reads exist in the SDK's or @relaycast/sdk's dist JS, so the env var is only a convention and must be passed explicitly.
facts.source: grep over pkg/package/dist and rcx/package/dist; agent-relay.js:21-27

facts.question: Q1. Does hosted setup need an account or payment?
facts.answer: The API lists POST /workspaces with no auth. The docs say the CLI is free and open source and that the desktop app is the paid upgrade. No docs page states any account, payment or quota requirement for hosted workspaces made through the SDK or init --hosted. Solo init explicitly says no account is required. Actual behaviour of hosted creation without sign-in was not tested.

facts.question: Q1. Which server does a key belong to?
facts.answer: SDK default baseUrl is `https://cast.agentrelay.com`. Without the desktop app, `init --hosted` creates workspaces on `https://armadillo.agentrelay.com` with `ar_ws_*` keys. With the desktop app installed it uses cast, and armadillo keys are refused on that machine. API doc: hosted `rk_*` keys stay on cast. The SDK adds `/v1/...` itself, so baseUrl must have no /v1 suffix. Whether @relaycast/sdk 8.16 works end to end against armadillo is unverified.
facts.source: rcx/package/dist/client.js:91; docs/full.txt:1238-1240; docs/relaycast-api.md:12-18; rcx/package/dist/agent.js send path

facts.question: Q2. How does a long-running process register an identity?
facts.answer: `relay.workspace.register<T extends AgentLike | AgentLike[]>(agents: T, options?: RelayRegisterOptions): Promise<T extends AgentLike[] ? RelayAgentClient[] : RelayAgentClient>` and `reconnect(input: { apiToken: string }): Promise<RelayAgentClient>`. Registration is create-only: an existing name is rejected with `name_conflict` (HTTP 409) with or without strict, and the token is returned once. The returned client exposes `.token`. Recovery of a lost token: `relay agent rotate <name>` or POST /agents/{name}/rotate-token.

facts.question: Q2. Can one process hold several identities?
facts.answer: Yes. register accepts an array, and each token gets its own client through clientsByToken. Each client is added as a source to one workspace-level fan-in, so relay.addListener sees all of them, and cross-source copies of one event are collapsed. A handler is not told which local identity received the event, so route on envelope content.

facts.question: Q3. How do you create and join a channel, and post?
facts.answer: `channels.create(input: RelayCreateChannelInput): Promise<RelayChannel>` with `{ name; topic?; metadata? }`, `join(name: string): Promise<void>`, `invite(channel: string, agent: string): Promise<void>`. Post: `sendMessage(input: RelaySendMessageInput): Promise<RelayMessage>` with `{ to: string | string[]; from?; text?; msg?; mentions?; mode?; attachments?; blocks?; idempotencyKey?; metadata?: Record<string, unknown> | null }`. `to` is '#channel', '@handle' or an array for group DM. Sends require an agent client; the workspace-key client has none. CreateChannelRequestSchema on the client accepts any string; server-side name rules and the error code for a duplicate channel are unverified.

facts.question: Q3. How do you receive messages?
facts.answer: Callback over WebSocket. `relay.addListener<K extends keyof RelayEventMap>(selector: K, handler: ListenerHandler<RelayEventMap[K]>): () => void`. Calling it opens the stream lazily. The socket is per agent at `/v1/node/ws`. A workspace key alone cannot receive, so at least one agent must be registered or reconnected. Polling exists too: `channels` messages via `messages.list(channel, { limit?, before?, after? })`, plus durable `inbox.list` and `inbox.subscribe`. Outbound webhooks exist via POST /subscriptions.

facts.question: Q3. What does a received message look like?
facts.answer: Handler receives `{ type: 'message.created', message: RelayMessage, envelope: RelayEventEnvelope }`. RelayMessage: `{ id, messageId, kind?, text, from: { id?, name? }, target?, channel?: { id?, name? }, conversationId?, threadId?, parentId?, mode?, createdAt?, updatedAt?, metadata?, blocks?, attachments?, replyCount?, reactions?, readByCount?, mentions? }`. RelayEventEnvelope: `{ from?, to?, channel?, parent? }`. Thread replies arrive as a separate 'thread.reply' event, so do not reply in threads if listening only to message.created.

facts.question: Q4. Are payloads text only?
facts.answer: No. Send accepts `metadata: Record<string, unknown> | null`, sent as wire `data`, and normalize maps it back to `message.metadata`. `text` is still required on the wire. Limits on metadata size are unpublished. Reads via REST normalization are confirmed in code. Survival through the node-ws deliver transform was not exercised, so put the envelope in both metadata and text. `message.reaction`-style attachments and blocks exist but are not needed.

facts.question: Q5. Minimum applicant code against the real types?
facts.answer: Written to relay-applicant.ts and register-once.ts. Both pass tsc --strict against @agent-relay/sdk@15.0.1 with @relaycast/sdk@8.16.0. Neither was run against a live workspace.
facts.source: tsc run in research/relay/tc: tsc_exit=0, reg_tsc=0

facts.question: Q6. Delivery guarantees and duplicates?
facts.answer: Node delivery is at-least-once; the source comment says so. Frames carry per-agent seq and the SDK auto-acks them (`autoAckDeliveries: true`). The client dedupes redelivered events by `type:id` in memory, which resets on restart. A successful send confirms enqueue only; read receipts confirm consumption. Reconnecting nodes replay unacked work, per the API doc. App-level dedupe is still needed.
facts.source: rcx/package/dist/ws.js:344-362,386-398; rcx/package/dist/agent.js:162; messaging/types.d.ts RelayMessageMode comment; docs/relaycast-api.md WebSockets section

facts.question: Q6. Ordering?
facts.answer: The stream has a monotonic per-agent `agent_seq`, and inbox.list replays in FIFO order. There is no documented cross-sender or per-channel ordering guarantee, so use revision numbers, not arrival order.

facts.question: Q6. Rate limits?
facts.answer: No numbers appear in the docs or README. The client recognises 429 and `rate_limited`, honours Retry-After capped at 60 s, and retries by default on 429, 500, 502, 503, 504 with maxRetries 3, backoff 1 s, multiplier 2. A `backpressure` code also exists.
facts.source: rcx/package/dist/client.js:26-32,202-203; rcx/package/dist/errors.js:6,26,35; grep of docs/full.txt returned no limit values

facts.question: Q6. Version stability, and is @next needed?
facts.answer: @next is not needed for the SDK or for the CLI's sake of version: dist-tags for both @agent-relay/sdk and agent-relay are latest 15.0.1 and next 15.0.1-next.0, so next is older. The docs still print `agent-relay@next` for the CLI, and following them is harmless. 15.0.0 was published 2026-10-31T14:46Z and 15.0.1 at 17:19Z, today, with next releases several times a day, so churn is high. facts.question: Q7. What happens to a post when Relay is unreachable?
facts.answer: The promise rejects with `RelayError`, code `transport_error`, retryable true, message 'Network request failed: fetch failed'. Against a closed local port: register failed in 9 ms, reconnect in 7129 ms, send with no key in 4686 ms, send with a key in 6922 ms. Nothing is queued locally for later delivery. Every send carries an Idempotency-Key, auto-generated if absent, so sends are always retried.

facts.question: Q7. What about a hung host or a dropped socket?
facts.answer: client.js passes no AbortSignal or timeout to fetch, so a black-holed host waits on Node's own limits; wrap sends in a timeout. A Promise.race timeout does not cancel the in-flight retry, so a post reported as failed can still land later. WebSocket reconnect uses 1 s to 30 s backoff, and a circuit breaker at 30 attempts stops it permanently, surfaced as a `permanentlyDisconnected` event on the events surface. After that no messages arrive until reconnect or restart. onError or a console warning reports listener errors.

facts.answer: openai latest is 7.47.0; zod latest is 4.6.7. The openai peer range is zod "^3.25 || ^4.0". zodTextFormat detects v4 through the _zod property and uses z4.toJSONSchema. facts.question: Q3: Which schema shapes fail locally in the SDK?
facts.answer: .optional() alone throws: 'uses .optional() without .nullable() which is not supported by the API'. z.record throws: 'must set additionalProperties: false'. .nullable().optional() passes and is emitted as required and nullable. .default('a') does NOT throw: it emits {default:'a'} and the field is required. Avoid .default(); whether the API rejects it is unverified. Use .nullable() only.

facts.question: Q3: What are the documented strict-mode limits?
facts.answer: All fields must be required. additionalProperties:false is required on every object. The root must be an object and not anyOf. Up to 5000 object properties, 10 nesting levels, 1000 enum values across all enums, and 120,000 total characters of names and enum values. minimum, maximum, exclusiveMinimum, exclusiveMaximum, multipleOf, minItems, maxItems, pattern and format are supported, except on fine-tuned models. allOf, not, dependentRequired, dependentSchemas, if, then and else are unsupported. anyOf is allowed below the root. Our schema compiles to 36 properties, all 10 objects closed and fully required, with minimum/maximum emitted on confidence.

facts.question: Q4: How should the shape be reshaped for strict mode?
facts.answer: Use one slot per field: {status: stated|user_unknown|not_mentioned, value: T|null, confidence: 0..1}. Fixed object keys replace the free-key confidence map. toPatch() rebuilds patch, the confidence map, unknownFields and missingFields in code. ledgerType counts as missing only when attached is stated true. The schema passed zodTextFormat and $parseRaw locally.

facts.question: Q5: How do refusal and incomplete behave in responses.parse?
facts.answer: The Responses path does not throw on either. parseResponse parses only when status is completed, so incomplete gives output_parsed null and the code checks status plus incomplete_details.reason. A refusal is a message content item with type 'refusal' and also leaves output_parsed null. Mocks confirmed both.

facts.question: Q5: Which errors are worth catching?
facts.answer: ZodError, thrown from parse when the schema does not match; the mock confirmed it for the bad-intent payload. SyntaxError is caught as a precaution but was not exercised. RateLimitError was mocked with a 429. APIConnectionTimeoutError and the APIError base are exported from openai and caught, but not exercised by the mock. LengthFinishReasonError and ContentFilterFinishReasonError come from the chat-completions path and do not apply to responses.parse.

ANSWER: 42 inches minimum, not 36. Guard height is 2025 California Residential Code (Title 24 Part 2.5) R321.1.2. A guard is required under R321.1.1 where an open-sided walking surface is more than 30 inches above the floor or grade below, at any point within 36 inches horizontally of the open edge.
Open sides of stairs: 34 in minimum, or 34-38 in where the guard top is also the handrail.
Decks reach this through R507.10, because R321.1.1's list does not say "decks".
Edition: the 2025 CRC applies to permit applications submitted on or after 2026-01-01 (BSC Bulletin 25-01, H&SC 18938.5). The prior edition, 2022 CRC, says the same thing at R312.1.1 / R312.1.2.
Numbering: R321 comes from the 2024 IRC, which shows guards at R321 on two state pages. In the 2025 CRC, R312 is now Minimum Room Areas, so citing R312 for a 2026 permit is wrong.
California amendment: the 2024 IRC says 36 in and the CRC says 42 in. That is why generic "36 in" sources are wrong for California.
San Jose: no guard amendment found. Part 2 of Chapter 24.09 (CRC Chapter 3) touches only R301.2 and R309. I read the 10/16/2025 draft ordinance, not final Ord. 31256.
CBC: 1015.2 / 1015.3 give the same 30/36 trigger and 42 in, but the CRC governs a single-family dwelling.
Confidence: high on 42 in, R321 and the trigger (mirrored code text plus government handouts agree); medium-high on no San Jose amendment. facts.question: What is the minimum guard height for a new residential deck on a San Jose single-family dwelling in 2026?
facts.answer: 42 inches (1067 mm). 2025 CRC R321.1.2, verbatim: "Required guards at open-sided walking surfaces, including stairs, porches, balconies or landings, shall be not less than 42 inches (1067 mm) in height as measured vertically above the adjacent walking surface or the line connecting the nosings." Exceptions: (1) "Guards on the open sides of stairs shall have a height of not less than 34 inches (864 mm) measured vertically from a line connecting the nosings." (2) "Where the top of the guard serves as a handrail on the open sides of stairs, the top of the guard shall be not less than 34 inches (864 mm) and not more than 38 inches (965 mm) as measured vertically from a line connecting the nosings."
facts.source: https://up.codes/viewer/california/ca-residential-code-2025/chapter/3/building-planning (third-party mirror, fetched 2026-10-31; saved dl/upcodes_crc25.txt line 6716). facts.question: When is a guard required?
facts.answer: 2025 CRC R321.1.1, verbatim: "Guards shall be provided for those portions of open-sided walking surfaces, including floors, stairs, ramps and landings that are located more than 30 inches (762 mm) measured vertically to the floor or grade below at any point within 36 inches (914 mm) horizontally to the edge of the open side. Insect screening shall not be considered as a guard." The trigger is strictly more than 30 in, and it is measured to the floor or grade at any point within 36 in of the edge, not only directly below the edge.

The 2025 CRC has the same numbering, so R312.1 is now "Minimum Area" for habitable rooms. The base 2024 IRC itself was not read directly.

I did not read the Chapter 3 adoption matrix or an HCD statement of reasons. HCD's 2024-cycle 45-day express terms, matrix and ISOR for Part 2.5 returned no R312, R321 or guard-provision hits (grep), which suggests the amendment carried forward unchanged, but that is also an inference.

facts.question: How does the CBC differ from the CRC on this question?
facts.answer: For this question the numbers match; the governing code differs. 2025 CBC 1015.2 uses the same more-than-30-in / within-36-in trigger, and 1015.3 reads "Required guards shall be not less than 42 inches (1067 mm) high". Its Group R-3 exceptions are limited to the open sides of stairs: 34 in, or 34-38 in where the guard serves as a handrail. Other differences are the section numbers and non-dwelling items in the CBC, such as occupiable roofs, mezzanines, and exceptions for stages and loading docks. The CRC is the governing code for a single-family dwelling; its scope is taken from secondary sources (Santa Cruz IB-900 applicability line and search results), since R101.2 / 1.1.3 was not read.

planImpact: Encode the guard height as 42 inches. Any plan, rule, fixture or demo text that uses 36 inches for a San Jose single-family deck is wrong: 36 is the model IRC value. plan.txt was not read for this lane, so whether it says this must be checked by whoever reconciles the lanes.

Cite CRC R321.1.1 and R321.1.2 for applications submitted on or after 2026-01-01. Do not cite R312.1.2 for those: in the 2025 CRC, R312 is Minimum Room Areas. Use R312.1.x only for 2022-edition applications submitted before that date. The height is 42 in under both.
Trigger logic is strict: guard required only when the drop is more than 30 in. Exactly 30 in does not trigger it.

Measure the drop to the floor or grade at any point within 36 in horizontally of the open edge. Deck height at the edge alone is not enough, because sloping grade can trigger a guard on a low deck. If intake collects only one deck height, the rule must flag that it cannot fully decide the trigger.

Compliance is height at or above 42 in, measured from the adjacent walking surface. Handle stairs separately: 34 in minimum on open sides, or 34-38 in where the guard top is also the handrail. Do not apply 42 in to stair guards or 34 in to the deck surface.
Link the deck rule to R507.10, which points to R321, because R321.1.1 does not name decks.
Do not cite the CBC (1015.2/1015.3) as the governing code for a single-family dwelling. Do not treat Dublin's CBC handout as CRC evidence.

Do not claim a San Jose local guard amendment, and do not claim a verified absence of one from the final ordinance. Say: none found in the 10/16/2025 draft Ord. 31256 text or the published Chapter 24.09 Part 2 section list.

Keep the permit exemption separate from the guard rule. The draft exemption covers detached R-3 decks of 200 sq ft or less, 30 in or less above grade at any point, not serving the required exit door. Being exempt from a permit is not the same test as R321.1.1.
Do not present a San Jose deck handout as a source: none was found. Do not label UpCodes or GoCodebook as official code text.

codeSnippets.title: 2025 CRC R321.1.1 and R321.1.2 (rule text to cite)
codeSnippets.code:
R321.1.1 Where Required: Guards shall be provided for those portions of open-sided walking surfaces, including floors, stairs, ramps and landings that are located more than 30 inches (762 mm) measured vertically to the floor or grade below at any point within 36 inches (914 mm) horizontally to the edge of the open side. Insect screening shall not be considered as a guard.

R321.1.2 Height: Required guards at open-sided walking surfaces, including stairs, porches, balconies or landings, shall be not less than 42 inches (1067 mm) in height as measured vertically above the adjacent walking surface or the line connecting the nosings.
